newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mostly lower after new high in Nov.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mostly lower after new high in Nov.

text.p: CME lumber futures showed early strength and posted a new contract high in November before slipping in a holiday shortened session to close mostly lower.

November tumbled at the start on profit taking and then rallied to post a new contract high of $484.40 per tbf before closing $1.40 lower at $482.30 per tbf. Other months ended $2.70 higher to $4.90 lower with January off $4.70 at $412.60 per tbf.
Profit taking and speculative long liquidation weighed on November at the start and profit taking was cited again late, partly on apparent reduced lumber demand, traders said.

Although most mills were closed for U.S. and Canadian holidays, demand for wood seems to be slowing due to the high mill asking prices. Also, snow and cold weather will start to slow user demand, they said.
"It looks like winter is starting early," one trader said.
Short covering supported deferreds early, but they also slipped on scattered pressure, traders added.

OSB closed mixed, off $2.00 to up $2.50 per msf (1,000 sq ft) with only January and March trading. January ended lower at $165.00 per msf at the early noon CST close in observance of the Veterans Day holiday.
